answer.rationale: Both activation and onboarding completion are down this quarter, and two independent memories (31, 86) point to onboarding simplification as a durable, low-risk lever for exactly this problem. Competitor entry pricing creates pressure to respond with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly documents that SMB discounting drove short-term signup/revenue gains at the cost of a 12pp retention hit, which conflicts with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective — this is flagged as a risk to resist reactively matching. I verify memory_73 to confirm the discount-harm finding is solid before ruling it out under competitive pressure, and memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-simplification evidence before committing the week's single experiment slot to it. Activation messaging (91) is a reasonable alternative but onboarding completion is further upstream and likely contributes to the activation drop, so fixing it may compound benefits. Enterprise and referral levers don't address the acute SMB/onboarding issue this week. Treating this as one experiment, not a proven rollout, preserves uncertainty for re-evaluation next cycle.
